first.rationale: Promotional pricing most directly addresses the immediate loss of price-sensitive SMB accounts, but memory_73 does not establish retention, customer quality, or long-term revenue durability. Memory_86 is the strongest alternative because it addresses the concurrent onboarding and activation declines, yet its evidence is limited to early adoption. Verify both before committing; absent stronger downstream evidence, use a guarded, targeted pricing test with qualified-revenue and retention guardrails.

final.rationale: Run a shortened-onboarding experiment. The verified record directly addresses the current onboarding decline and showed higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention. Reject promotional pricing for this slot because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% retention decline and failure at the first renewal, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Longer-term revenue impact from onboarding remains uncertain, so use retention and qualified-revenue guardrails.
